name: Anime cel shading
doc: The picture as an anime TV frame: flat cel fills in 2-5 tone bands (cool lavender shadows, a white shine band, the bass pushing the light across the bands), clean ink lines from its luma edges (thicker on a kick), and the camera punching in on every kick toward a new point like an action cut; onsets deal fresh focus lines and sparkle stars, a run of onsets thickens the falling sakura, the drop paints an anime sky over the bright top and lights a lens flare, and the first kick of some bars is an inked impact frame. With nothing picked it draws its own subject (sky, sun, a cumulus, ridges, a hill with a sakura tree and a power pole) and cel-shades that.

palette.doc: grade of the bands, the shadow tint, ink, flare and sparkle colours

options: auto (draw one when nothing is picked)
subject.doc: auto suits core-media as the input; use 'the input' on any other image

bands.doc: tone bands (fractional values move the band edges)

soft.doc: ramp between bands: 0 = hard cel, more = smoother

light.doc: exposure into the bands (bind a follower: the lighting jumps bands)

pump.doc: the bass and the kicks push the light up

grade.doc: fills pulled to the palette by band

shadow.doc: how cool (lavender) the shadow bands go

shine.doc: flat white band on the brightest parts

ink.doc: ink line width, pixels (a kick thickens it)

ink_sense.doc: how faint an edge still gets a line

punch.doc: how far the camera punches in on a kick

space.doc: beats between kicks (bassy onsets closer than this are one kick)

lines.doc: focus lines on onsets (and some during the drop)

petals.doc: falling sakura (a run of onsets doubles them)

drop.doc: the drop look: sky gradient and lens flare (bind core-section's drop)

impact.doc: chance a bar opens with an inked impact frame on its first kick
